newsitem.title: USA: CME March lumber futures close limit up again.
newsitem.headline: CME March lumber futures close limit up again.

text.p: CME March lumber futures closed up the daily limit of $10.00 per thousand board feet for the second consecutive day on short covering, traders said.
March closed up the limit at $413.50 per tbf with May up $3.90 at $391.20 and other months up $0.80 to $3.50 per tbf.
Carryover short covering and technical support was evident from the start. Higher financial futures and talk of a possible firmer tone to cash adding to demand, they said.
"They (mills) are reporting a little better activity in spruce," one trader said.
However, only 17 buy orders remained unfilled at the close.

Technically, the market also looks higher. Futures recently held a triple bottom at $392, basis March, before the rally which started on Thursday. The market looked oversold after falling $45 in two week, they said.

They added that lower cash prices were already in the market. Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $396 per tbf, down $8 from midweek and $18 under last Friday's level. They also said the Random Lengths Framing Lumber Composite posted its first drop of 1997.
